core_obligations: If 0 lies in S then (a, s) is equivalent to (0, 1) for every pair, so S^{-1}A is the zero ring (proof line 1333).
Conversely, if 0 is not in S then 1/1 and 0/1 differ in S^{-1}A, so the localisation is not the zero ring (proof line 1334).
proof_roadmap: Run the definition of the localisation's equivalence relation with 0 in S to collapse all classes (proof line 1333).
In the other direction, exhibit 1/1 and 0/1 as distinct when 0 is outside S (proof line 1334).
difficulty_reason: The lemma characterises the collapse of a localisation: S^{-1}A is the zero ring if and only if 0 lies in S (statement lines 1327-1330). Both directions are settled directly from the equivalence relation that defines the localisation, without any computation with the ring structure: with 0 in S every pair (a, s) is equivalent to (0, 1), and with 0 outside S the two classes 1/1 and 0/1 stay distinct (proof lines 1332-1335). The content is recognising that the collapse condition is exactly membership of 0 in the multiplicative subset, which is the kind of step a reader must supply; the author states both directions in full. H2.
